overall_assessment.realism: The samples are highly realistic, reflecting common credential harvesting tactics such as typosquatting domains with character substitutions, use of recently registered domains from high-risk countries, failed SPF/DKIM checks, and capturing credentials via POST requests. The inclusion of detailed technical data like email headers, SMTP logs, DNS lookups, web server access logs, and network packet captures adds to the authenticity. The scenarios cover multiple attack vectors including phishing emails and smishing, with plausible social engineering narratives targeting payroll and cloud storage services. The use of valid SSL certificates on compromised domains and realistic user agents further enhances credibility.
overall_assessment.consistency: The samples maintain strong consistency and adhere well to the expected schema. Each entry includes a scenario description, comprehensive technical data with relevant fields, indicators of compromise, detection methods, and associated MITRE ATT&CK techniques. The structure and field naming are uniform across samples. Timestamp formats, IP addresses, domain names, and log snippets are consistently formatted. Minor variations in email clients and user agents are appropriate for realism and do not break schema uniformity.
suggestions: Include explicit fields for email DKIM and DMARC results in the technical_data to complement SPF results for completeness.
